stories.headline: US resumes intelligence sharing with Ukraine on Russian strikes, Zelensky says

sources.body:
US special envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss proposals on ending Russia's years-long conflict with Ukraine.

The talks come one day after Witkoff's meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo, which a US official described as "constructive".

Kyiv previously accused the US of withholding key intelligence - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by Washington - but on Tuesday, Zelensky said that intelligence sharing with the US on Russian missile attacks "works now".

Zelensky and his European allies said it was now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo when Witkoff meets Putin on Wednesday.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb, who also took part in the talks, said "genuine progress" was made on proposals to achieve peace but gave no details and warned that patience would be needed.

Witkoff was not present at the joint press conference after Tuesday's talks in the Norwegian capital. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, another key envoy, took part in the meeting via video link.

A US official later described the talks as "very productive and constructive", saying there was a "strong alignment at the working level" among the US, Ukraine and Europe on "the next steps".

The official confirmed that Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin in Russia tomorrow to discuss the proposals and that Kushner will again participate virtually.

Putin is yet to publicly comment on the latest developments, but Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov earlier said the Kremlin would listen to what Wiktoff would offer, while ruling out "any political concessions".

Relations between Ukraine and the US have soured in recent weeks to the extent that Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".

Ahead of next month's US midterm elections, Trump has also sought to blame Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have been rising since the start of the US-led war on Iran.

Speaking after Zelensky's news conference in Oslo, Trump again told reporters at the White House he wanted Kyiv to "make a deal". He said Russia would like to "get it done" and it was "time for Ukraine to end this war".

Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

Russian drone attacks have continued this week. Ukrainian officials said at least 10 people were killed on Tuesday - four in Kyiv and the capital region, another four in the eastern Donetsk region, and two in the central city of Dnipro. Another attack overnight on Wednesday killed two more people near Kharkiv, the country's second-largest city.

Addressing the issue of US intelligence sharing after Tuesday's talks, Zelensky said he was "thankful that intelligence works now".

"Speaking about early warning, which is very important for our people, our children, adults, civilians because we can hear when ballistic[s] is coming - so we are thankful to American side, now it works, it's great," the Ukrainian president said.
sources.headline: Zelensky says US intelligence sharing 'works now' after talks with Trump envoy

sources.body:
Advance warnings of missile attacks were seemingly suspended last week by the White House, but Ukraine’s president says: ‘Now it works’

The US has resumed sharing intelligence with Kyiv about Russian missile strikes, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday after a meeting with the US envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway.

He said Ukraine was again receiving advance warnings of ballistic missile attacks, which were seemingly suspended last week by the White House. “Now it works. It’s great,” he said, adding that the US move would save lives.

The Ukrainian president said: “It’s very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians, because we can hear when ballistic [missiles] is coming. So we are thankful to the American side.”

Witkoff will on Wednesday meet Russian president Vladimir Putin after what a US official called “constructive” talks with Zelenskyy in Norway . The US envoy would aim to “create a pathway toward direct trilateral and broader multilateral negotiations”, a US official told Reuters.

The talks in Oslo took place amid the worst crisis in US-Ukraine relations since Putin’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago. Donald Trump has bitterly accused Zelenskyy of failing to end the war and has said Ukraine needs a new leader.

On Tuesday Trump again suggested Zelenskyy was the main obstacle to an agreement. “We want Zelensky to make a deal. He can make a deal. He could have made a deal two years ago when we had our little chat in the Oval Office ,” he said.

Trump also said he had asked Putin to release Stephen Hubbard – an American taken prisoner by Russian forces in occupied Ukraine – in a further sign of his growing public alliance with Moscow.

The US president’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, joined Witkoff and Zelenskyy by video for the talks. Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, and the Finnish president, Alexander Stubb, also took part, alongside EU and British security officials.

Zelenskyy said he had held a “positive” phone call earlier with the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio. Asked if Ukraine was now losing the war, after recent hostile US actions, Zelenskyy replied: “Of course we are not losing. But we are losing people because of Russian attacks and time. It’s a pity.”

He said he had raised with Rubio restrictions imposed last week on Starshield, the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s satellite internet service. The slowdown has crippled Ukraine’s ability to launch mid-range drone strikes on Russian battlefield positions.

Zelenskyy said he had offered to stop Ukraine’s long-range attacks on Russian oil refineries – a key Trump demand – if the US provided Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. The Pentagon has blocked the delivery of Patriots to Kyiv paid for by other countries, leaving Kyiv more vulnerable than ever to air attacks.

Speaking on Tuesday, Zelenskyy also said he opposed a trilateral summit floated by Putin, which would see the Russian leader, Trump and China’s president, Xi Jinping, meet next month to strike a Ukraine deal. Zelenskyy would be shut out, the Wall Street Journal reported .
sources.headline: US has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine about Russian strikes, says Zelenskyy

stories.headline: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads beyond Kenya

sources.body:
Nigeria has recorded a case of Ebola in a female patient who travelled from Uganda in East Africa to Abuja, capital of the West African state.

Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the diagnosis had been confirmed by laboratory tests.

The patient is in isolation and receiving medical care after being admitted to a hospital in Abuja.

Health authorities have begun contact-tracing to prevent further spread, with 44 close contacts of the woman identified.

Nigeria, the first West African state to report a case linked to the current Ebola crisis in East Africa, successfully stopped a previous outbreak in 2014.

Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo, which began in May, has claimed at least 4,600 lives, with more than 9,500 cases recorded, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reports .

It was caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Shortly after the outbreak was announced, it was also reported in Uganda, where at least two people died. Uganda declared itself free of the disease in August after its last patient was discharged.

The disease has also spread to Kenya, which has reported at least nine infections.

On Monday, the US advised its citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya because of health risks and raised its travel advisory level for the country.

Since the outbreak, Nigeria has stepped up disease surveillance, with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control issuing public health advice to travellers.

The agency says travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission may be required to complete a health declaration form. Those arriving from other countries are currently exempt.

It has also urged travellers to remain vigilant and seek medical attention promptly if they develop symptoms of Ebola.

In 2014, Nigeria managed to beat an outbreak of Ebola which caused at least eight deaths.

Go to BBCAfrica.com for more news from the African continent.

Follow us on Twitter @BBCAfrica , on Facebook at BBC Africa or on Instagram at bbcafrica
sources.headline: Nigeria confirms Ebola case linked to East Africa

sources.body: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case in Africa's latest outbreak, while Kenya reported its ninth infection, raising fears of further spread across the continent. Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya warned of an “extremely serious threat” and urged the international community to send funding, medical supplies and health workers.
sources.headline: Nigeria records first Ebola case as outbreak spreads across Africa

stories.headline: Italy deploys 500 troops and tightens security measures after Milan riots

sources.body:
Government planning tougher security measures as France also says military forces will be deployed

Italy’s government is sending 500 soldiers to Milan and vowed a “firm response from the state” after protests against the cost of living descended into clashes with police, vandalism and looting. Further demonstrations are planned on Saturday.

The government of the far-right prime minister, Giorgia Meloni , also announced new security measures, including an offence of violent participation in ⁠a demonstration, tougher penalties for ⁠rioters, and financial liability for ​parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.

In France , the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said on Tuesday some military forces would be deployed during ⁠protests ​planned for this Saturday, “mostly to free police and gendarmes in their mission to maintain order”.

The French prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, told parliament that the police presence during Saturday’s demonstrations ⁠would be “massive” and that ​his ​goal was ​for an “immediate return ​to order” ‌after last weekend’s violent riots.

Lecornu will meet with representatives from five unions on Wednesday morning to discuss security, according to a letter sent to the organisations and reviewed by AFP, which noted some were attempting to subvert the protests with “unacceptable acts”. School students have not been invited to the meeting.

Police in Milan, in northern Italy, detained 271 young people after hooded youths set bins ablaze, ransacked shops and smashed windows, including in the area surrounding the city’s cathedral, during the unrest on Saturday and Sunday.

Police used teargas and water cannon to disperse the violent groups, who were on the fringes of an initially peaceful protest. Of those detained, 32 have been arrested, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, police said on Monday. A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.

Images of Saturday’s clashes in France, including mobs looting shops and public buildings set on fire, prompted several countries including the US, China and Germany to issue travel advice for their citizens. Nearly 2,400 people were arrested in one of France’s most violent recent bouts of unrest.

French authorities on Monday announced partial curfews in several cities, including Paris, Bordeaux, Lille and Nice, and after a night of relative calm, Lecornu said on Tuesday that new curfews would be imposed where they were needed.

Authorities in Paris renewed Monday night’s curfew, which would apply from 11pm on Tuesday until 6am on Wednesday to the Place de la République, where many of the weekend clashes took place, and in the central Les Halles shopping district.

Paris police ordered a temporary ban on people carrying cans or bottles of petrol or gas, and banned masks and helmets in some areas. A man was also arrested in connection with the burning down of the historic town hall in Limoges .

The Italian press agency Ansa reported that one of the security measures being considered in the country was aimed at second-generation immigrant youths, known as maranza – a slang term used to describe gangs of young people, usually from marginalised areas.
sources.headline: Italy to deploy 500 troops to Milan after days of protests and looting

sources.body: Italy announced tougher security measures on Tuesday after weekend riots in Milan left more than 100 police officers injured and shops looted. The government will deploy 500 additional soldiers, impose harsher penalties for violent protesters and hold parents financially responsible for damage caused by minors.
sources.headline: Italy announces new security measures after Milan riots, deploying 500 soldiers

stories.headline: US says an Iran peace deal is extremely difficult as attacks disrupt shipping through Hormuz

sources.body:
At least 15 vessels struck in waterway in past 10 days, with rumours that they were carrying valuable goods

People have been scouring the strait of Hormuz for spilt cargo after Iran attacked at least 15 container ships passing through the crucial waterway in the past 10 days.

Some ships have been hit by drones, others by mines. On Sunday, a ship was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade launched from a small boat 75 miles (120km) north-east of the Saudi port of Jubail.

The rise in Iranian attacks appears to have helped resolidify Tehran’s disputed control over the strait, as well as pushing the price of a barrel of Brent crude oil close to $108 a barrel on Monday morning.

Last Wednesday a ship travelling from Karachi, Pakistan, to Fujairah, in the United Arab Emirates , sunk after hitting a mine, according to Iranian state TV. All 21 crew members were evacuated and no injuries were reported. Dozens of its 2,500 containers were seen floating in the water. Rumours that iPhones and other expensive goods were among its cargo – fuelled by fake AI-generated photos published on social media – prompted fishers and others to investigate.

One fisher told an Iranian reporter: “The Arab boatmen, who were closer to the ship, arrived earlier than the Iranians. They used stonecutters to cut the container and took whatever was there.”

Col Javad Mokhtar Rezaei, the deputy head of cultural and social affairs for Iran’s cyber police (Fata), told the Tasnim news agency: “In some cases, the phones offered may actually exist, but exposing electronic components to salt water and extreme humidity can cause corrosion of internal components, damage to the boards, battery and display, and cause hidden malfunctions in the device’s performance.”

Meysam Doost-Mohammadi, a spokesperson for the Iranian mobile phone Aassociation, said it would be unusual for valuable devices to be transported by ship.

The bulk of the recent attacks have occurred close to the coast with Oman , a route that Iran regards as unauthorised. In the seven days to Friday 16 October, 12 vessels were attacked, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO).

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps ( IRGC) says it has the right to attack any ship that seeks to traverse the strait without its permission or with its transponders off. Officials have also ordered local fishers not to pillage the sea for luxury items, saying the goods are the property of the state.

Two oil tankers were hit on Saturday, including a supertanker carrying 2m barrels of oil, according to the IRGC. The Fars news agency published a video that appears to show the tanker burning, but which cannot be independently verified. A third tanker was hit late on Sunday.

It is disputed how many ships have been hit by mines or IRGC shelling. UKMTO’s weekly overview recorded 254 transits of the strait (125 outbound, 129 inbound) in the week to 14 October, approximately 70% below pre-conflict levels.

Dr Devaraj Asir Ramesh, of Anna University in Chennai, India, warned that the region’s marine habitats faced threats from toxic debris and oil spills, while noise might have disturbed marine life. Iranian strikes on the Emirates, he said, were likely to have contaminated seagrass beds with hydrocarbons and caused auditory damage to cetaceans – marine mammals such as dolphins and porpoises – which are sensitive to loud noise that travels through the sea.
sources.headline: People scour strait of Hormuz for spilt cargo after Iran attacks container ships

stories.headline: Boeing's 737 Max 10 receives final FAA certification after years of delays

sources.body: Boeing's largest 737 Max jet has cleared a major regulatory hurdle, with US aviation authorities approving the Max 10 for passenger service on Tuesday after nearly a decade of delays. The certification marks a boost for the planemaker's recovery, with deliveries expected to begin in 2027.
sources.headline: Boeing's 737 Max 10 finally wins FAA approval after years of delays

sources.body: The US Federal Aviation Administration has given final approval for the 737-10, the largest model in Boeing's best-selling Max family. The certification comes more than five years after the narrowbody jet's maiden flight, and marks an important step for the planemaker that's been trying to regain ground following a safety and management crisis. Plus, the French government has offered all businesses affected by the recent riots a interest-free loan of up to 50,000 euros.
sources.headline: US regulators certify Boeing 737 Max 10 after years of delay

stories.headline: Lula seeks Bolsonaro's disqualification in Brazil runoff over alleged Meta algorithmic interference

sources.body:
Lula and Bolsonaro spar in Brazil’s fiery first presidential run-off debate

Both candidates for the Brazilian presidency have called for the disqualification of their rivals over allegations of social media interference, ramping up political drama ahead of the close-fought October 25 runoff election.

Brazil’s right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has requested the annulment of the candidacy of his rival, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, over what he called unlawful propaganda.

Lawyers for Bolsonaro filed a request with the Superior Electoral Court on Tuesday, alleging Lula’s “abuse of power” in the mass dissemination of government postings during the campaign period via WhatsApp.

Bolsonaro’s camp claimed the Brazilian government sent mass messages to millions of Brazilians via the messaging service, promoting social programmes, benefits and government initiatives in the midst of the presidential race, Brazilian media reported.

The request to the electoral court seeks to declare Lula and Social Communications Minister Sidonio Palmeira ineligible to hold public office for a period of eight years.

In the other camp, Lula’s campaign said on Tuesday that it would request the disqualification of Bolsonaro on Wednesday over alleged election interference by WhatsApp parent company, the tech giant Meta.

Lula’s petition, which has yet to be officially filed, alleges “algorithmic manipulation” by Meta aimed at harming Lula’s chances of winning, a campaign source told AFP.

The electoral court had given Meta 24 hours on Monday to prove it was complying with an order to treat both campaigns equally, threatening a daily fine of around $200,000 if it didn’t.

The order came after Lula’s campaign alleged that Meta, which owns Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, was suppressing his online content to boost Bolsonaro.

“We have completed the implementation of the measures to comply with the Superior Electoral Court’s decision,” the company said on Tuesday.

Lula and Bolsonaro are locked in a heated presidential race after the right-wing candidate, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, won the initial round of voting earlier this month with 47 percent of the vote to the incumbent’s 45 percent.

Polls show a very close race ahead of Sunday’s runoff round.
sources.headline: Lula, Bolsonaro seek to disqualify each other ahead of Brazil runoff

sources.body: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign is preparing to request the annulment of right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy over alleged social media interference from US tech giant Meta as Brazil’s presidential race intensifies ahead of Sunday’s runoff. The petition that will be submitted to the country's top electoral court claims "algorithmic manipulation" by Meta to suppress Lula's campaign content and boost Bolsonaro.
sources.headline: Lula's campaign seeks to disqualify Bolsonoro from Brazil presidential vote over Meta 'interference'

stories.headline: Trump announces $8 billion farm-aid plan in last-minute bid to bolster Republicans

sources.body: Republicans locked in tight races this November are desperately hoping the Trump administration’s last-minute gambit to send farmers $8 billion in taxpayer money will work. President Donald Trump announced the new round of money, aimed at farmers struggling with high diesel prices, during a Monday rally for at-risk GOP Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas. The move comes as White House officials have scrambled to address anger in farm states from Republicans. Trump’s decisions to import more foreign beef , his tariff regime and high fuel costs amid the Iran war have riled already strained farmers and ranchers — a key GOP voting bloc. Farmers won’t know how much money to expect for several more weeks. Even then, if approved, they won’t receive the payments until late November or early December at the earliest, according to three people close to the plans, granted anonymity to share details. With two weeks to go before the election, the new aid may also arrive too late to convince some voters. But top Republicans are banking on the announcement to stem GOP bleeding in farm states — especially in the Midwest, where Marshall, GOP Senate nominee Ashley Hinson in Iowa and GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers in Michigan have been struggling in their election campaigns. In some cases, they've broken with Trump publicly on high prices and the war. “This will go a long way to making sure the folks that feed us have it a bit easier when they most need it,” said Rep. Derrick Van Orden, referring to the farmers in his district. The Republican is locked in a highly competitive race in a rural-heavy stretch in Wisconsin’s 3rd District. However, the internal USDA taxpayer-funded account Trump is tapping for the payments doesn’t actually have enough money in it right now to make the payments, meaning Congress will have to approve the new funds or the administration will have to take it from another program, according to three Trump officials who were granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. Marshall — who’s facing a tougher-than-expected reelection campaign in deep-red territory — and Rep. Austin Scott (R-Ga.) were among the Republicans who helped push for the $8 billion, according to the three Trump officials. Marshall requested the administration allocate money to assist farmers with spiked fuel costs in a letter to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins in September. “Roger Marshall is the leader who fought for that to happen,” Trump said during the Monday rally. Spokespeople for Marshall and for Scott did not respond to requests for comment . The White House referred POLITICO to USDA’s announcement on the money. USDA spokesperson Harry Fones said in a statement that the aid package is Trump’s “latest action to deliver” for farmers and the department is actively reviewing the data to determine payments. Trump’s decision also comes after administration officials realized the president’s previous step to make off-road dyed diesel more widely available had limited benefits for farm country over other options, according to two of the Trump officials and another administration official involved in the matter. Top agriculture lobbyists further warned the dyed diesel plan could actually backfire on farmers , because they could still be required to pay taxes on the product — just further down the road. So, Trump officials settled on the $8 billion tranche of direct money for farmers, given that similar kinds of payments to farmers — dating back during the president’s first trade war in 2018 — have quelled enough farmer and rural voter anger to shore up necessary support for Republicans during election season. Trump officials and Republican operatives in the Midwest are banking on the money shoring up support again this cycle — especially for GOP voters who are angry but also don’t want to vote for Democrats. Trump heads this Thursday to Iowa — where top Republicans have been worried about internal polling that warned several weeks ago they could lose all three Iowa House races, key Senate races and other once-safe red seats across farm states. "It's going to help bring farmers' votes out," Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) told POLITICO of Trump’s plan on Tuesday. "This is some way that the federal government can step in to help farmers for problems that they face through no fault of their own,” he said. Most Hill Republicans weren’t given a heads-up about Trump’s announcement, including appropriators, and many hadn’t received any details from USDA as of Tuesday morning, according to two people familiar with the conversations who were granted anonymity to share private details. Top agriculture groups have warned they’d need at least $50 billion in direct aid this fall to make farmers whole following the impacts of tariffs, weather-related disasters and other high costs linked to the Iran war’s chokehold on agricultural supplies. Farm-state Republicans are pushing to add at least $12 billion in direct farm aid payments to a separate year-end legislative package. Monday’s aid rollout followed a number of other funding announcements made in swing rural districts. The White House doled out a first round of $12 billion in bailout funds earlier this year for growers of top agricultural commodities who were hit hard by Trump’s tariff agenda. Alongside Republican Senate candidate Mike Collins in Georgia, Rollins announced a $3.3 billion loan to build a power plant last week. Rollins rolled out $180 million in funding for seed research alongside vulnerable Iowa Reps. Zach Nunn and Marianette Miller-Meeks earlier this month. Trump also said he would approve long-derailed permanent year-round sales of ethanol during the Kansas rally — which would be a critical boon for corn growers across the Midwest. But the move has been long-stalled in Congress. “With Roger Marshall in the Senate, we will make year-round E15 permanent. But if Adam Hamilton is in, I’m not doing it,” Trump said. “That’s a big deal for Kansas, actually.” Rachel Shin contributed reporting.
sources.headline: Trump just made a last-minute gambit to save farm-state Republicans in the midterms

stories.headline: Poll finds voters associate Republicans with Big Tech tax breaks as data-centre backlash grows

sources.body: Americans are fed up with data centers and Big Tech, and Republicans are poised to take more of the political blame in the Nov. 3 midterms. The POLITICO Poll found last week that Americans were far more likely to associate the GOP with giving tax incentives to tech companies at a time when the public’s concerns about artificial intelligence and data center sprawl are only deepening. Nearly half of respondents — 47% — called Republicans the party of tech tax breaks, more than double the 21% who said the same for Democrats. Voters are also far more likely to want candidates who propose stripping away tax incentives for the data centers needed to fuel the AI boom, according to the new poll, conducted by PF Global. About a fifth of respondents said that ending those tax breaks would be among their most important tax issues in the midterms, while only 1 in 10 wanted to offer new preferences for data centers. The top tax priorities for voters, according to the poll, are hiking taxes on billionaires and curbing breaks for big companies. The findings come as lawmakers in both parties have scrambled to respond to the growing voter concerns over AI and data centers — and as Americans increasingly associate Silicon Valley titans with the Republican Party. But in both Democratic and Republican-led states alike, governors have sought to put new limits on tax incentives that were already approved for data centers. Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) rolled out a proposal last week that would take that a step further by imposing a 100% tax on any state or local incentive offered to AI data centers. But it’s Democrats who have gone more on the offensive about the issue. Former Sen. Sherrod Brown, for instance, has made data center incentives a key issue as he tries to unseat Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), a former state lawmaker and lieutenant governor. “Jon Husted’s ‘deals’ gave wealthy tech companies a windfall and left Ohioans footing the bill,” Brown recently posted on social media. Democrats have specifically homed in on Meta , which has cut its tax liability in recent years by billions of dollars as it builds out its AI products. And they have sought to tie expanded tax breaks approved by Republicans in last year’s megabill to the increase in data center construction. The GOP enacted incentives for companies in a broad array of industries as part of the 2025 tax cuts. But Big Tech has found those tax breaks particularly useful , helping to drive a big decrease in corporate tax payments as AI spending keeps trending upward. Meanwhile, Democrats with 2028 ambitions have floated new taxes on AI companies, while Democratic lawmakers have teed up legislation that would keep data centers from taking advantage of incentives like Opportunity Zones and bonus depreciation, both of which Republicans expanded in 2025. In fact, Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) recently gave last year’s megabill another new name in a recent debate with his opponent, Rep. Mike Collins (R-Ga.). “I want to know if you will commit to voting to repeal that data center tax scam that you voted for,” Ossoff said. It’s not clear how much the current anti-AI energy will lead to new legislative limits in the coming months. But the new poll found Americans have a real fear of the unknown with artificial intelligence. A majority of respondents said that tech chief executives had been secretive about the potential risks of AI, while a plurality of Americans believe both that the risks of artificial intelligence development outweigh the benefits and that the government should strictly regulate the emerging technology.
sources.headline: Poll: Voters see Republicans as the party of Big Tech tax breaks

stories.headline: Alaska Republicans fear a same-name candidate and ranked-choice voting could cost Senator Dan Sullivan his seat

sources.body: ANCHORAGE — Alaska Republicans have railed for years against ranked-choice voting. Now some worry it could cost them in a critical Senate race. GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan is facing not only well-known former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola in the four-way general-election field, but a same-name challenger who Republicans think could siphon votes from him in the close contest. Some GOP operatives fear the senator will lose first-choice votes to retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan Jr. — and that supporters of his longshot rival might not rank the incumbent at all in the state’s unusual election system where voters can pick backup options that get counted if no candidate clears 50% of the initial vote. Two recent polls that simulated ranked-choice tabulations showed Peltola as the victor. Art Hackney, a Sullivan ally who runs a super PAC boosting the senator, said Dan J. Sullivan is “going to get a percent of the vote” and warned it could “potentially” be "significant in terms of impacting" the result of the race. "Sullivan can win ... but it makes it a heck of a lot harder,” added a Republican operative working on other Alaska races. “It’s what the race is going to come down to: If he loses, it'll for sure be because of that. And if he wins, it'll be in spite of that." Republicans have for years bemoaned the system that allows voters to rank their preference and eliminates candidates until one reaches a majority as “costly” and “confusing,” and argue it has undercut their party . Top Republicans like outgoing GOP Gov. Mike Dunleavy and President Donald Trump have urged voters to repeal the system via a ballot measure this fall after a previous effort failed two years ago . “Even if he gets a percent or 2% or 3% percent with the phony ranked choice stuff, you never know what they're going to do with it,” Trump said of Dan J. Sullivan in a rally in Wasilla last week, adding that it “could be the difference.” It’s happened before: Peltola benefited in her House win from a split GOP field, while Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) warded off a Trump-backed challenger in 2022 partly because of ranked-choice voting. Alaska Republicans are also fretting about the governor’s race this year, where three GOP candidates are competing, urging voters to “rank the red.” Dan J. Sullivan, Heikes and Peltola’s campaign did not respond to requests for comment. The similarly named Sullivans are separated on the ballot by their middle initials and party affiliation (the incumbent is listed as a Republican, the challenger without a party). But the senator and his allies aren’t taking any chances. They’re employing several of the tactics Murkowski used during her successful 2010 write-in campaign, including giving out rubber wristbands branded with the senator’s name and party affiliation, and airing a radio jingle with the NRSC . "Dan S. is your No. 1," the jingle goes. "If he’s not, rank him second, don’t throw your vote away. Dan S., Daniel, Gerry — just don’t rank Mary." "Dan S. Sullivan has two opponents in this race: Democrat Mary Peltola, and the ranked choice system she and her allies have deceptively manipulated to her advantage,” said Nate Adams, a spokesperson for the senator. “But our campaign is confident that Alaskans aren't confused. They know the real Dan, and we're making sure every voter can find him: ballot facsimiles on every mailer, voters reached at the door and on the phone, and even a jingle.” Those pushing to keep ranked-choice voting in Alaska argue the system helps mitigate the so-called spoiler effect. The group behind this year's repeal measure said in an email that it's a nonpartisan effort focused solely on eliminating the system. Outside GOP groups boosting Sullivan like Americans for Prosperity Action and Club for Growth Action have been urging voters at doors and via mailers to rank the incumbent first, a slightly different approach than Sullivan’s campaign. “Make Republican Incumbent DAN S. SULLIVAN your 1ST CHOICE and ONLY CHOICE,” read one Club for Growth Action mailer seen by POLITICO. “In a tight election, it doesn't take a ton of people to get confused to possibly change the trajectory and the outcome,” said Kevin Greene, senior adviser for AFP Action in Alaska. A version of this article first appeared in POLITICO Pro’s Morning Score. Want to receive the newsletter every weekday? Subscribe to POLITICO Pro .
sources.headline: The weird reasons why Alaska Republicans are so worried about their Senate race

stories.headline: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker invests heavily in Black and Hispanic candidates ahead of a possible 2028 run

sources.body: CHICAGO — JB Pritzker is pouring tens of millions of dollars of his own money into boosting Black and Hispanic candidates this cycle. That could help him win over critical voters in 2028. The billionaire Illinois governor — who’s also considered a potential presidential contender — is investing at least $38 million in battleground races, according to a person familiar with the governor’s political strategy granted anonymity to discuss details. Much of that spending has gone to candidates of color, some of whom haven’t drawn much other investment from national Democrats. Pritzker is also investing in races in all six early states on the Democratic presidential nominating calendar, which was rearranged earlier this year to give prize spots to five states with significant Black or Hispanic communities: South Carolina, Nevada, New Mexico, Virginia and Michigan. Asked by POLITICO about how his midterms spending could lay the groundwork for a presidential campaign, Pritzker said he’s “focused on winning in 2026.” But some of those receiving major infusions from Pritzker say it should earn him a serious look in 2028. “Governor Pritzker is playing a very important role” in the party, said Rep. Shomari Figures, a Black Democrat facing an uphill fight in Alabama who has gotten an assist from Pritzker’s newly formed super PAC, Ready for the Fight. “He actually cares and is … willing to invest in districts where minority candidates have a good shot if they have the right type of support. I think that's an important element of any leadership.” Pritzker said Ready for the Fight’s strategy focuses on GOP-leaning districts that would normally be “out of sight for Democrats” but have become competitive in a favorable midterm environment.   Figures is fighting for reelection in a district Republicans redrew to make it harder for a Democrat to win by decreasing the Black population, after the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act this past spring . When that court decision came down, Figures said Pritzker was one of the first people to call him to offer help. “The fact that he reached out and engaged us through that lens with that level of knowledge about what was happening in Alabama meant a lot to us,” Figures said. Pritzker is spending $1.6 million for Figures, $1.9 million to boost Tennessee state Rep. Justin Pearson, another Black candidate running in a newly gerrymandered district that includes part of Memphis, and has put $1.3 million behind Arkansas Democrat Chris Jones in his race against Rep. French Hill (R-Ark.) in Little Rock, making him the largest Democratic spender besides the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee in all three districts. Pritzker is also the largest individual donor to Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa’s gubernatorial campaign, personally contributing $200,000 before committing another $1 million earlier this month. The latter donation came around the same time the Democratic Governors Association also contributed $1 million. Hispanic officials and lawmakers have been ramping up the pressure on the group’s chair, fellow 2028 hopeful Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, to invest more in Texas. Pritzker called Hinojosa an “outstanding person.” “The opportunity for her to win and for Democrats to win as a result of her winning is tremendous,” Pritzker told POLITICO at a Thursday press conference. “From my perspective, we all ought to be helping somebody like that to overcome the odds.” And while he declined to criticize national Democrats’ strategic decisions not to spend for some candidates in tough races facing a deluge of GOP outside money, he made clear he was looking to make up for that lack of funding. “If I were running in one of those districts, and I’m not getting dollars that I see going to other districts, I would feel frustrated,” Pritzker said. “There's only so much you can do when you're being outspent 3 to 1 or 4 to 1 nationally, and so I'm trying to do my best to fill in some of that wherever I can.” Pritzker is not the only potential 2028er looking to woo politically powerful Black and Hispanic communities, and his day job and his own reelection bid keeps him away from the national trail — unlike some of the other senators and governors who’ve been crisscrossing the country for months. But what he lacks in time, he makes up for in money. His spending strategy is catching the attention of senior Black Democratic leaders. “People tend to take notice of the people who take notice of them,” said South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn. Clyburn said he takes Pritzker “seriously” as a potential presidential candidate but cautioned that Black voters and organizers in his home state, where Pritzker recently addressed the state NAACP’s annual convention, likely won’t be swayed by campaign contributions alone. “We are going to take measure of candidates, not based upon how deep their pockets are, but we're going to take measure of how deep their commitments are to those things deemed important in the African American community,” he said. Still, the donations are helping the billionaire longtime Democratic donor and two-term governor forge new allies in key communities that could provide a boost come primary season. “I appreciate Governor Pritzker’s willingness to invest in places others have written off,” said Jones, who also thanked the DCCC for recently adding him to their list of targeted races. “Convincing people a race is worth investing in has often been an insurmountable barrier for Black candidates.” Pritzker’s PAC spent $2.8 million for New Mexico Democratic Rep. Gabe Vasquez, and the governor made a $400,000 personal contribution into a super PAC backing Nevada gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford, a Black candidate running in a heavily Hispanic early-voting state. But his biggest investment of the cycle was to boost Illinois Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton, who he picked as his 2018 running mate when she was a little-known state representative, then invested $10 million to help her win her U.S. Senate primary this spring. The move created some tensions: Pritzker’s endorsement of Stratton helped lift her 2026 Senate campaign significantly over two other candidates — including Rep. Robin Kelly (D-Ill.), another Black woman who has had a strained relationship with Pritzker over the years. That frustrated several members of the Congressional Black Caucus, though he’s sought to mend fences since. Clyburn, who endorsed and campaigned for Kelly, said that race won’t “dictate future relationships when it comes to putting our party in the best position to win the elections in 2028.” And ultimately, Stratton’s ascendance is a significant step in Pritzker's outreach to Black voters nationally. He will be credited with helping send just the sixth Black woman ever to the U.S. Senate after her likely victory in November. She could be a key 2028 surrogate should he run for president. “He really does have a platform to raise awareness of critical races that people might not otherwise pay attention to,” Stratton said. “I'm really grateful for that.” CORRECTION: An earlier version of this report misstated the nature of DGA's donations to the Texas governor's race; it was made independently from Pritzker's.
sources.headline: JB Pritzker’s midterm strategy wins the attention of Black and Hispanic Democrats

stories.headline: Spain's Supreme Court grants amnesty to Junqueras and three other Catalan independence leaders

sources.body: <p>El Tribunal Supremo ha aplicado este martes la amnistía al exvicepresidente de la Generalitat Oriol Junqueras y a los exconsejeros Raül Romeva, Dolors Bassa y Jordi Turull. Dos semanas después de que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html">el Tribunal Constitucional estableciera que la Sala Penal debió otorgar la medida de gracia al delito de malversación</a> que atribuyó a los exdirigentes independentistas, el Supremo ha cumplido este mandato y ha amnistiado a los cuatro antiguos miembros del Govern a los que juzgó y condenó por ese delito en 2019. La amnistía deja sin efecto la pena de inhabilitación que aún pesaba sobre ellos, por lo que los cuatro podrían ya presentarse a las próximas elecciones u ocupar un cargo público. En el auto en el que expone su decisión, el Supremo lanza al Constitucional un reproche insólito, por extenso y contundente. “Su innecesaria grandilocuencia revela el deseo de adornar un razonamiento invasivo del ámbito jurisdiccional que corresponde al Tribunal Supremo”, recalcan los jueces. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-20/el-supremo-asume-la-doctrina-del-constitucional-y-amnistia-a-junqueras-y-tres-exconsejeros.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El Supremo amnistía la malversación a Junqueras y tres exconsejeros con fuertes críticas al Constitucional

sources.body:
El Tribunal Supremo ha resuelto este martes aplicar la ley de amnistía al exvicepresident de la Generalitat y líder de ERC, Oriol Junqueras , y a los exconsellers Raül Romeva, Jordi Turull y Dolors Bassa tras el aval del Tribunal Constitucional al perdón de la malversación. Los cuatro líderes del procés fueron condenados por este delito.

La Sala de lo Penal expone en un auto al que ha tenido acceso RTVE que esta decisión viene dada porque el Constitucional le ordenó amnistiar a los dirigentes independentistas y en el que se declara extinguida la responsabilidad criminal derivada de la sentencia del procés.

A pesar de ellos, los magistrados critican en el auto "la innecesaria grandilocuencia" del Constitucional , que "revela el deseo de adornar un razonamiento invasivo del ámbito jurisdiccional" del Supremo.

El pasado 7 de octubre el Constitucional remitió al Supremo la sentencia que avala amnistiar el delito de malversación a los líderes del procés. La mayoría progresista del Constitucional consideró que se había vulnerado el derecho a la tutela judicial efectiva y observó incoherencias por parte del Supremo, al que recrimina que adoptase una decisión contraria al espíritu de la norma.

Los exlíderes del procés podrían volver a presentarse a unas elecciones porque ya no pesa sobre ellos la inhabilitación. En la sentencia del Supremo constaba condenas por inhabilitación hasta los años 2030 y 2031.

De hecho, Esquerra ya ha anunciado que Oriol Junqueras, Raül Romeva y Dolors Bassa cerrarán las listas de as generales tras dejar de estar inhabilitados. En la formación se muestran "satisfechos" por la amnistía y creen que "se ha hecho justicia".

"Hoy es un día de victoria, de celebración, tras nueve años de represión que nunca tuvieron que haber existido ", ha expresado Oriol Junqueras ante la sede de ERC en la capital catalana, en una atención a los medios de comunicación. Y se ha referido a su inhabilitación, que queda sin efecto y que, por lo tanto, permite que pueda volver a su puesto de trabajo en la universidad. "Hoy hay dos niños que recuperan a un padre que puede volver a ejercer de profesor en la universidad", ha remarcado.

" Hoy la política vuelve al terreno de la política y sale de la judicialización ", ha dicho Junqueras, al mismo tiempo que dice que la represión vivida "demuestra que nos tienen mucho miedo, y hacen bien de tenernos ese miedo".

Turull , en declaraciones a los medios desde la sede de Junts en Barcelona, ha celebrado este paso que ha tildado de "acto de justicia". Asimismo, ha insistido que con la aplicación plena de la amnistía " no se cierra el conflicto político ".

A diferencia de Junqueras y otros políticos de ERC, Turull ha rechazado que vaya a estar en las listas de las elecciones del 29-N. "No me mueve esto, es una lectura del indepdendentismo frente al a por ellos, eso es lo que menos me interesa ahora mismo", apuntado.

Carles Puigdemont también se ha pronunciado en redes. " Arrastrando los pies, tarde y refunfuñando… pero el Supremo no tiene más remedio que firmar la capitulación . Han dedicado tiempo, recursos y capacidad de invención para evitarla, pero la amnistía llegará a todo el mundo", ha remarcado.

stories.headline: PP and Vox negotiate Senate coordination for Spain's November election

sources.body: <p>El Partido Popular y Vox aproximan posiciones para concurrir con más fuerza al Senado en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha confirmado este martes que ambas formaciones negocian en estos momentos para <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-18/un-frente-de-izquierdas-y-otro-de-derechas-se-disputaran-a-cara-de-perro-el-control-del-senado.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-18/un-frente-de-izquierdas-y-otro-de-derechas-se-disputaran-a-cara-de-perro-el-control-del-senado.html">encontrar una fórmula que les permita lograr una mayoría más holgada</a> frente a la papeleta conjunta de PSOE y Frente Amplio. Una vez cerrado el plazo para presentar coaliciones, el viernes pasado, PP y ultras barajan otros planes. En una entrevista en Cope, Feijóo ha apuntado como escenario más plausible el de que los ultras no se presenten en determinadas circunscripciones y que el Partido Popular ceda senadores por designación autonómica como contrapartida. El líder del PP quiere un pacto, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-17/vox-baraja-no-presentarse-al-senado-en-algunas-provincias-para-evitar-una-mayoria-de-izquierdas.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-17/vox-baraja-no-presentarse-al-senado-en-algunas-provincias-para-evitar-una-mayoria-de-izquierdas.html">mete presión a Santiago Abascal</a> y busca con ese planteamiento controlar los tres quintos de la Cámara alta, lo que le permitiría hacer nombramientos sin tener que pactar con el PSOE. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-20/feijoo-confirma-negociaciones-con-vox-para-las-listas-del-senado-si-estan-a-la-altura-el-pp-tambien.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Feijóo plantea ceder senadores autonómicos a Vox para que no se presente en algunas circunscripciones

sources.body:
Después de las próximas elecciones generales habrá pactos entre PP y Vox . Así lo ha admitido, en una entrevista en la Cadena Cope, el presidente popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo , que ha recogido el guante lanzado por Santiago Abascal para ir conjuntamente en las listas del Senado.

Para Feijóo "sería un error facilitar al sanchismo el control directo o indirecto del Senado". La alternativa es negociar con los de Abascal, conversaciones que ha asegurado se llevan a cabo con "discreción y respeto" . "Si Vox está a la altura el PP también lo estará", ha dicho y ha confirmado que "se buscarán fórmulas de acuerdo". Con ello podrían alcanzar una mayoría de tres quintos que permitiera a ambas formaciones hacer algunos nombramientos como por ejemplo elegir los cuatro vocales del Tribunal Constitucional que le corresponden a la Cámara Alta sin el concurso de la izquierda.

En este sentido, ha recordado que los cinco senadores que tiene Vox fueron designados por parlamentos autonómicos en los que tienen acuerdos tras los últimos comicios. Ya hay una "experiencia" , ha admitido, y un " marco de negociación con Vox que ha funcionado ". Ahora, ha asegurado, hay aún "mayor confianza y mayor responsabilidad". Y al igual que son esos pactos autonómicos, los futuros para la Cámara Alta serán "transparentes": "Los pactos encapuchados se los dejamos al PSOE, la izquierda y Bildu", ha remarcado.

Desde Vox, José María Figaredo , no ha querido detallar el acuerdo que ambas formaciones tienen sobre la mesa, pero ha asegurado que su partido hará "lo que haya que hacer". Ha prometido que actuarán con "responsabilidad y altura de miras" y siendo conscientes de que el objetivo es "sacar a este gobierno mafioso de la Moncloa".

A diferencia del Congreso, donde se votan listas cerradas y bloqueadas, en el Senado los ciudadanos eligen directamente a los candidatos mediante listas abiertas , en un sistema que prima especialmente a la fuerza más votada, que suele obtener tres de los cuatro escaños en juego por provincia, mientras que el cuarto queda en manos de la segunda.

En concreto, 208 de los 266 senadores que integran actualmente la Cámara Alta son elegidos por sufragio directo . Los otros 58 son designados por los parlamentos autonómicos, a razón de uno por comunidad y otro más por cada millón de habitantes, respetando la representación proporcional de las fuerzas políticas en cada asamblea legislativa.

El PSOE se ha unido a toda su izquierda para intentar ser primera fuerza e invertir la aritmética parlamentaria del Senado, donde la pasada legislatura el PP gozó de una holgada mayoría absoluta gracias a ser la lista más votada. Feijóo y Abascal buscan ahora la vía para evitar la dispersión del voto e impedir que la alianza de las izquierdas logre su meta.

La fecha límite para alcanzar un acuerdo es el lunes, cuando termina el plazo para presentar las listas electorales. Feijóo ve "posibilidades de llegar a puntos de encuentro" .

Preguntado por la ley de nietos y el estudio sobre la misma que está realizando el Tribunal Constitucional, Feijóo asegura que el texto, que no es una ley sino una instrucción, " es un fraude y una ingeniería electoral clarísima ". Por ese motivo se ha mostrado convencido de que el desde el tribunal de garantías "no se atreverán a dictar una resolución a sabiendas injusta".

stories.headline: Constitutional Court is expected to reject an appeal over overseas voting rights under the descendants law

sources.body: <p>Una mayoría de los doce magistrados que componen el Tribunal Constitucional defenderá este miércoles que se inadmita el recurso de amparo presentado por el Defensor del Pueblo, según fuentes del órgano de garantías. El recurso pedía restablecer el derecho al voto de más de 160.000 españoles, nacionalizados en virtud de la <i>ley de nietos</i>, que viven en el extranjero y a quien el Tribunal Supremo ha retirado cautelarmente el sufragio a poco más de un mes de las próximas elecciones generales. La mayoría del Pleno, sin reflejar esta vez la división de referencia entre progresistas y conservadores, considera que como el Supremo abrió un plazo de alegaciones para los afectados —vigente hasta el viernes, 23 de octubre—, el recurso del Defensor es prematuro y no cumple con el requisito de subsidiariedad del amparo: esto es, que se haya agotado la vía de la justicia ordinaria. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/el-constitucional-se-dispone-a-rechazar-el-amparo-presentado-por-la-ley-de-nietos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

stories.headline: Barcelona and Catalonia create a public company to rehabilitate 4,000 structurally troubled homes in Besòs-Maresme

sources.body: L’oposició ha reprovat la tinenta d’alcaldia d’Urbanisme, Laia Bonet , per les rehabilitacions de pisos del barri del Besòs i el Maresme . Segons denuncien els veïns són defectuoses . El suspens polític a Bonet s’ha produït a la Comissió d’Ecologia, Urbanisme, Mobilitat i Habitatge d’aquest dimarts a la tarda i ha estat a proposta de BComú amb el suport de Junts , el PP i Vox , l’abstenció d’ ERC i els vot en contra del govern del PSC . BComú ha impulsat la iniciativa perquè els veïns que viuen en finques que ja s’han rehabilitat denuncien defectes en les obres executades , com ara acabats poc polits, rajoles trencades, goteres, finestres que no tanquen i avaries en ascensors i intèrfons. Es tracta dels veïns dels 10 primers blocs (d’uns 200 que s’han de rehabilitar per problemes estructurals) on s’hi va començar a actuar fa cinc anys en el marc d’una prova pilot. Tret d’un bloc on els treballs van acabar fa tres anys, a la resta les actuacions encara estan en marxa. També et pot interessar Rehabilitacions defectuoses al Besòs: Laia Bonet s’exposa a un suspens polític de l’oposició Roger Torres i Liñán 2 minuts de lectura Salt d’escala en la regeneració En la mateixa comissió també s’ha aprovat inicialment la constitució de l’empresa pública Impulsem Futur Besòs Maresme, SA , compartida entre Ajuntament de Barcelona i Generalitat de Catalunya, amb participació majoritària del consistori. Un òrgan que ha de servir per fer “ un salt d’escala “, ha dit Bonet, en la regeneració de pisos del barri. Gràcies a la creació d’aquesta empresa mixta, en els pròxims anys s’injectaran 415 milions d’euros al Besòs i al Maresme per rehabilitar tot el parc d’habitatges que, ara com ara, té problemes estructurals greus i pisos amb estances apuntalades . Per Bonet l’acord és “important” perquè el model actual d’actuació ha quedat demostrat que és “limitat”. “Se n’han rehabilitat 192 habitatges en quatre anys, hem d’esperar 40 anys més per rehabilitar el barri?”, ha dit. També et pot interessar Ajuntament i Generalitat encarrilen la regeneració del Besòs: 415 M€ per rehabilitar 4.000 pisos Jaume Planagumà Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: L’oposició reprova Laia Bonet per les rehabilitacions del Besòs i el Maresme

sources.body:
Un bloque afectado por aluminosis en el barrio del Besòs i el Maresme, en Barcelona. / MANU MITRU

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha aprobado este martes crear la empresa que compartirá con la Generalitat de Catalunya para impulsar el plan anunciado en 2020 y que ha cosechado un resultado demasiado escaso hasta ahora para rehabilitar bloques del barrio del Besòs i el Maresme, gravemente afectados por la aluminosis y otros daños estructurales que comprometen la comodidad y la seguridad de los vecinos. La fundación de la sociedad ya se anunció en mayo pasado , el consistorio la dotará con 265 millones a lo largo de los próximos 12 años y el Govern, con 150 millones . En el vecindario, donde se concentran algunas de las calles donde se declaran menos rentas en la capital, se diagnostica que 4.000 pisos requieren de remodelación. “Con el plan actual, se han reformado 192 viviendas en cuatro años y tardaríamos más de 40 años a acabar con el ritmo actual” , ha estimado la teniente de alcalde Laia Bonet, en la comisión municipal de urbanismo.

La nueva estrategia, a desarrollar en los próximos 12 años, diagnostica que 1.800 pisos de 84 comunidades son los que se hallan en peor estado, con deficiencias muy severas , mientras que los daños de otros 650 se juzgan severos y se catalogan como leves en 1.550, que requieren de una rehabilitación básica. La memoria económica de la empresa pública mixta dibuja dos escenarios: reformar todos los pisos afectados sin echar abajo ninguno, que es la única opción contemplada hasta ahora, y una segunda hipótesis con un coste de 270 millones de euros que plantea el derribo de las 1.800 viviendas más degradadas y la construcción de 1.500 hogares para vecinos con derecho a realojo, mientras que otros 300 no tendrían derecho a ese traslado.

Esa suposición plasmada en el documento económico de la sociedad mixta ha originado un encontronazo entre Barcelona en Comú y el PSC. La concejala Lucía Martín (BComú) ha culpado al ejecutivo de Jaume Collboni de querer derribar “medio barrio” y desalojar a vecinos sin alternativa. Bonet le ha acusado de mentir . “Hay diversos escenarios, solo ha subrayado uno como si solo hubiera uno, se contemplan diferentes escenarios para valorar la viabilidad de la empresa”, ha indicado la teniente.

Fuentes del gobierno municipal han subrayado que, a día de hoy, la única posibilidad que se tiene sobre la mesa es remodelar los 4.000 domicilios y que no se propone derruir viviendas en el barrio. Atribuyen la alusión a una eventual demolición de los 1.800 domicilios más deteriorados en el estudio económico a una hipótesis que definen como tan solo teórica a efectos de elaborar el proyecto financiero de la sociedad. Justifican que los economistas han de tenerla en cuenta junto a la de la reforma plena de las viviendas para valorar si la futura sociedad pública es viable. También han reducido a un supuesto teórico que el análisis plantee edificar 1.500 pisos para reubicar a vecinos y negar el derecho de realojo a 300 hogares.
sources.headline: Barcelona aprueba crear una empresa con la Generalitat para desencallar la rehabilitación de 4.000 pisos en el Besòs

stories.headline: Catalonia keeps digital whiteboards in early-childhood classrooms but removes open internet access

sources.body: (ACN/Redacció) Educació no retirarà les pissarres digitals de les aules d’I3, I4 i I5 , com va anunciar que faria el juny del 2025 , però en suprimirà els “usos lliures” i no tindran connexió a internet . Així es desprèn de l’actualització del Pla de digitalització responsable que ha publicat la conselleria i que planteja un model d ‘ús “pedagògic, restringit i segur” . Ho ha avançat El Periódico i ho han confirmat fonts d’Educació a l’ACN. Tot plegat coincideix amb la petició d’accelerar les mesures per reduir les pantalles als centres educatius . També et pot interessar Illa es referma en la limitació de l’accés a la IA i aposta per recuperar els llibres a les aules Andrea Muñoz 2 minuts de lectura Ús pedagògic, restringit i segur de les pissarres El document, titulat Les pissarres educatives a l’educació infantil , planteja un model d’ús “pedagògic, restringit i segur” d’aquests recursos. “La pissarra digital no ha de ser una pantalla d’ús permanent. S’ha d’utilitzar quan aporti valor a l’activitat educativa compartida (afavorir la conversa, el llenguatge oral, l’observació conjunta, la creativitat, l’escolta, els projectes col·laboratius i la construcció compartida del coneixement)”, indica el text. Alhora, remarca que se n’ha de controlar el temps d’ús i insisteix que “ la tecnologia no substitueix l’experiència educativa ”, sinó que és el docent qui, seguint el seu criteri pedagògic, ha de decidir quan utilitzar-la de manera limitada i intencionada per enriquir la pràctica a l’aula. També et pot interessar L’ús de pantalles, un problema de salut pública que pot provocar “danys irreversibles” Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura Tres nivells d’accés i un perfil infantil La conselleria crearà un perfil específic d’usuari, anomenat infantil , amb funcionalitats limitades i un entorn simplificat, que evitarà les distraccions i la sobreestimulació visual dels alumnes d’I3, I4 i I5. A més, establirà tres nivells d’accés : el del docent, protegit amb contrasenya i amb accés a totes les funcionalitats multimèdia; el de l’administrador, amb accés complet per gestionar la pissarra, i el de classe, amb accés directe, però amb les limitacions esmentades. Així, amb el perfil infantil no es podrà navegar lliurement per internet i només es podrà accedir a recursos autoritzats. Tot plegat coincideix amb la petició d’accelerar les mesures per reduir l’ús de pantalles als centres educatius que Aixeca el cap ha fet aquest dimarts davant la Comissió d’Educació del Parlament. La plataforma ha advertit que “ no n’hi ha prou amb prohibir els telèfons mòbils als instituts” i ha reclamat una revisió “immediata” de tots els dispositius digitals que Educació proporciona a l’alumnat. També et pot interessar Adolescència Lliure de Mòbils, sobre les xarxes socials: “Els hem donat una eina perillosa” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 2 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: Catalunya manté les pissarres digitals a infantil, però n’elimina l’ús lliure i l’accés a internet

sources.body:
En junio de 2025, la consellera Esther Niubó anunció que las tabletas y las pizarras digitales desaparecerían "progresivamente" de las aulas de educación infantil , con el objetivo de alcanzar las "pantallas cero" en I3, I4 e I5 . Los dispositivos, explicó entonces, serían "reubicados en otros espacios de los centros". A los pocos días, sin embargo, las direcciones de las escuelas recibieron un correo electrónico en el que el propio Departament les indicaba que no tocaran las pantallas . El motivo era que los equipos se habían adquirido con fondos europeos Next Generation EU y había que estudiar si las condiciones de financiación imponían obligaciones de mantenimiento y permanencia durante un periodo determinado.

Según ha podido saber EL PERIÓDICO , una vez analizadas estas condiciones, la conselleria ha llegado a la conclusión de que no puede retirarlas y ha publicado este lunes una actualización de su Plan de Digitalización Responsable que sustituye el compromiso de eliminar las pantallas en infantil por la supresión de sus " usos libres" .

La nueva directriz establece que la pizarra digital "debe ser un recurso educativo puntual ". El cambio de criterio llega apenas tres años después de que la conselleria, encabezada entonces por Josep Gonzàlez-Cambray, destinara cerca de 90 millones de euros para desplegar paneles digitales en los centros educativos, con unas condiciones de financiación que ahora impiden su retirada.

El nuevo documento titulado 'Las pizarras educativas en educación infantil' plantea un modelo de uso "pedagógico, restringido y seguro" de estos dispositivos. "La pizarra digital no debe ser una pantalla de uso permanente. Debe utilizarse cuando aporte valor a la actividad educativa compartida (favorecer la conversación, el lenguaje oral, la observación conjunta, la creatividad, la escucha, los proyectos colaborativos y la construcción compartida del conocimiento), y debe controlarse su tiempo de uso ", apunta la nueva publicación, que insiste en que la tecnología "no sustituye la experiencia educativa", sino que el docente, siguiendo su criterio pedagógico, decide cuándo utilizarla de forma limitada e intencionada para enriquecer la práctica en el aula.

Para asegurar el cumplimiento de esta función, la conselleria señala que creará un perfil específico de usuario, denominado 'Infantil' , con funcionalidades limitadas y un entorno simplificado, evitando distracciones y sobreestimulación visual para los alumnos de I3, I4 e I5. Se establecen tres niveles de acceso: el docente, mediante contraseña, dispondrá de todas las funcionalidades multimedia; los administradores tendrán acceso completo para gestionar la pizarra; y el nivel de clase tendrá acceso directo, pero con las restricciones mencionadas anteriormente.

Así, con el perfil infantil no se podrá navegar libremente por internet (no se podrá pinchar un vídeo de Youtube para tranquilizar a los niños cuando vuelven revoltosos del patio). Solo estará permitido acceder a recursos autorizados, principalmente del entorno EDU365 (actividades interactivas y talleres, por ejemplo) y de la biblioteca de actividades JClic , que fomentan las habilidades de expresión y comprensión oral, potencian la atención, la concentración, la memoria, la percepción visual, la autonomía, la autocorrección, la identificación de relaciones o diferencias entre elementos y la iniciación en la lectoescritura; detallan.
sources.headline: Catalunya no retirará las pantallas en educación infantil, aunque limitará su uso y no tendrán internet

stories.headline: Barcelona offers Sareb up to €4 million for the Raval site occupied by the Àgora Juan Andrés Benítez

sources.body: L’ Ajuntament de Barcelona ha ofert a la Sareb (Societat de Gestió d’Actius Procedents de la Reestructuració Bancària) entre 3,5 i 4 milions d’euros per comprar el solar on hi ha l’ Àgora Juan Andrés Benítez , al Raval. El tinent d’alcaldia d’Urbanisme, Jordi Valls, així ho ha explicat durant la Comissió d’Ecologia, Urbanisme, Mobilitat i Habitatge d’aquest dimarts, 20 d’octubre. Valls ha explicat que “encara l’ operació no està tancada però sí que hi ha una oferta formal “. Cal recordar que sota aquest solar, ubicat al carrer de l’Aurora, número 13, hi havia una ordre de desallotjament prevista per al 15 d’octubre però que es va suspendre després que l’Ajuntament fes l’oferta als propietaris del solar. Pendent de la resposta de la Sareb Valls ha revelat que l’Ajuntament està en espera de saber la resposta de la Sareb a l’oferta municipal i també de quin serà el preu final de l’operació. Així mateix, el tinent d’alcaldia d’Urbanisme ha explicat que “l’ ús de l’espai es decidirà més endavant si bé el que se sap és que aquest solar té capacitat per a 20 o 25 habitatges “. Les diferents entitats que fan ús de l’espai sempre han defensat que els agradaria que el solar continués tenint un ús comunitari però que el que consideraven més important és que fos un ús públic. 12 anys de lluita veïnal L ‘ espai està ocupat des del 5 d’octubre del 2014 . La data no va ser aleatòria. Es complia el primer aniversari de l’homicidi imprudent del veí i activista del barri Juan Andrés Benítez a mans de vuit mossos d’esquadra. Des de llavors l’espai el gestionen un grup d’entitats del Raval que asseguren que han convertit el solar en un punt de cohesió i referència al barri. El desallotjament del 15 d’octubre era el quart intent de la propietat de recuperar el solar. També et pot interessar S’atura el desallotjament de l’Àgora Juan Andrés Benítez, l’Ajuntament presenta una oferta de compra Àngels Molina 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: L’Ajuntament ofereix a la Sareb prop de quatre milions d’euros pel solar Àgora del Raval

sources.body:
El Ágora Juan Andrés Benítez, en el barrio del Raval, en Barcelona. / FERRAN SENDRA

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha presentado una oferta de 3,5 millones a cuatro millones de euros a la Sareb para comprar el solar del Raval donde se instala la Ágora Juan Andrés Benítez, el espacio ocupado por distintos colectivos que ofrecen actividades a los vecinos y sobre el que pesa una orden judicial de desalojo . El teniente de alcalde de Vivienda, Jordi Valls, ha explicado este martes en una comparecencia a instancias del PP en la comisión municipal de urbanismo que la adquisición y su precio aún no están cerrados, ni tampoco hay una decisión tomada sobre qué hará el consistorio con la parcela, en el número 13 de la calle Aurora. “Sobre a qué uso se destinará el solar, es una decisión que se tomará más adelante, pero tiene capacidad de edificabilidad de 20 a 25 viviendas” , ha estimado Valls.

El teniente ha argumentado que “el Raval se caracteriza por una escasa disponibilidad de suelo para vivienda o zonas verdes” . “La adquisición en el barrio es positiva para la administración pública”, ha defendido Valls. El socialista ha recordado que el ayuntamiento trataba con el Gobierno de España incorporar los activos de la Sareb al patrimonio municipal antes de que se planeara que los bienes del llamado ‘banco malo’ -surgido a raíz de la crisis inmobiliaria de 2008 y el posterior rescate bancario- pasen a manos de la nueva agencia estatal de vivienda, Casa 47.

Valls ha explicado que lo que el ayuntamiento pretende es una “compra directa”. “ Hace tiempo que hablamos con la Sareb -ha sostenido Valls-. No es una decisión improvisada, hacía tiempo que hablábamos con la Sareb”. Por su parte, la popular Sonia Devesa ha pedido aclaraciones sobre los “criterios” del gobierno del alcalde Jaume Collboni “para comprar inmuebles con dinero de todos los barceloneses” . En ese sentido, el PP ha discutido las razones para adquirir el solar de la calle Aurora y también el bloque del número 74 de la calle Llenguadoc, en el barrio de Sant Andreu. En ese segundo caso, la operación se anunció el mismo día en que se preveía el desalojo de las 18 familias residentes en el bloque, con 32 personas, incluidos seis menores .

Devesa ha subrayado que se trata de propiedades ocupadas ilegalmente. “¿Para comprar vivienda, hace falta ocuparlas y hacer ruido mediático? Eran colectivos de activistas, no todos eran vulnerables ”, ha sostenido Devesa. Valls ha respondido que “ el ayuntamiento tenía la obligación de actuar con la Generalitat, fuese cual fuese la situación contractual de las familias”. Junts y Vox también han cuestionado las adquisiciones, mientras que los Comuns y ERC han defendido la decisión, al tiempo que han afeado los reproches del PP.

Valls ha recordado que la compra de Llenguadoc se ha vehiculado a través de un fondo de emergencia habitacional de la Generalitat, dotado con 25 millones de euros. “Es un fondo que se dedica a personas con riesgo de perder la vivienda y en situación dramática, como la que estaba esta finca”, ha postulado el teniente. Ha añadido que los informes que han resuelto que es pertinente comprar el inmueble de Sant Andreu están firmados por la Generalitat. El PP ha pedido saber cuándo se elaboraron los dictámenes y ha remarcado que, al mismo tiempo que se adquieren algunas fincas, hay demandantes de vivienda que llevan tiempo esperando un domicilio de emergencia o de protección oficial.
sources.headline: Barcelona calcula que pueden construirse de 20 a 25 pisos en el solar ocupado que quiere comprar en el Raval
